title: Teacher David Jones and wrist technique
summary: David Jones taught him to read; the rolls he picked up himself, playing from the wrist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Did you ever have a teacher?
David Jones. You would talk about David Jones. Sure. Well, David Jones was the man who liked me. But before David Jones, I was playing. Mm-hmm. What did he teach you?
He taught me how to read.
He taught me how to read. Mm-hmm. Well, where did you get your roles that you play? I mean, did you, did he teach
you those roles or did you pick them up by ear?

He didn't teach me no roles or nothing. I just picked that up. But you see some drummers, you know, when they played like this with their whole hand. Now you have them watching me, you never see them seeing my hand move. You see this wrist move. The wrist played direct from the wrist. That's how I played. That's the reason I was real so good.
Mm-hmm. So everything is in your wrist?
